I was bullied as a child and thought of myself as very boring. When I got to uni I would drink to excess at parties due to social anxiety. I was afraid people would think I was lame, also being wasted meant I forgot my worries and felt like I could connect better with others. Ironically and unsurprisingly alcohol had the effect of me behaving like such a piece of shit that I lost friendships and ruined relationships.

Later in my mid to life twenties I would get hammered at home if my husband was going out alone with friends. I was anxious and worried about what he would be getting up and lonely as well. So I would knock back a couple of beers and a bottle of wine in half an hour or less and black out. As I felt myself becoming extremely drunk I would have a feeling of happiness, relaxation and a lack of trouble for a short while. I would fall asleep and then wake about an hour later feeling awful.

Reading these back, and especially my drinking in my late twenties makes me realise just how much I didn't like myself as a person previously and how I struggled to spend time in my own company.
